query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_attitude_complaint
per_column.rationale: A text-derived binary flag for cabin-crew attitude complaints is squarely one of the 'cabin-service complaints' the query asks to isolate and correlate against Overall Rating. Samples support it: praise-heavy reviews (1,3,5) are False, and no crew complaint is fabricated. Genuine new grouping axis not present in the original numeric Staff Service score.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness_complaint
per_column.rationale: Distinct complaint category (responsiveness) that supports the 'most common complaint' ranking and its rating impact. Sample rows with attentive/regular service are correctly False; no unsupported True observed.

per_column.name: food_quality_complaint
per_column.rationale: A cabin-service complaint axis directly usable for the query. Reviews praising food ('plentiful and tasty', 'delicious') are correctly False; grounded reading of source text.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_complaint
per_column.rationale: Text-derived seat complaint flag. Partially overlaps the original numeric 'Seat Comfort' rating, but a binary complaint extracted from prose is a distinct signal fit for the complaint-elimination analysis. Sample 2 ('seats dreadful') correctly True, praise rows False — well grounded.

per_column.name: service_recovery_attempted
per_column.rationale: Not a complaint type itself, so it is tangential to 'eliminating the most common complaints', but it can still serve as a moderating axis (does recovery soften rating impact). Samples all False with no recovery language present — consistent grounding.

per_column.name: traveller_type
per_column.rationale: Trivially redundant with the existing original 'Type of Traveller' column (same category set: Solo/Couple/Family Leisure, Business), so it adds essentially no new analytical leverage for this complaint-vs-rating query. Values are not supported by the review prose in the samples (e.g. 'Excellent performance' → Family Leisure); presumed a passthrough of the original column, which keeps groundedness only moderate given the ambiguity.

per_column.name: flight_disruption_complaint
per_column.rationale: Disruption/delay complaints are a common driver of low ratings and a legitimate cabin/service complaint axis for the query. Samples (all smooth flights) correctly False; no invented disruptions.

per_column.name: inflight_entertainment_complaint
per_column.rationale: Text-derived IFE complaint flag; distinct from the original numeric 'Inflight Entertainment' rating and relevant to the complaint ranking. Sample 2 ('entertainment system dreadful') correctly True, praise rows False — strong grounding.

judge.rationale: The core of the added set is a coherent battery of text-derived complaint flags (crew attitude, responsiveness, food, seat, disruption, IFE) that directly enable identifying the most common cabin-service complaints and modelling their association with Overall Rating — exactly the axis the query needs. service_recovery_attempted is a reasonable moderating variable (moderately useful), while traveller_type is a near-duplicate of the existing 'Type of Traveller' column and adds little. Groundedness is strong: across all five evidence samples the complaint flags are sound readings of the review text (praise→False, explicit complaints→True) with no fabricated complaints; only traveller_type shows values unsupported by the prose, most plausibly a passthrough of the original column, which modestly caps table-level groundedness. Per the scope rule, no score was lowered for missing columns or coverage gaps.
